source_document.body:
El Teniente mine smelter. ( Image courtesy of: Codelco | Flickr. )
By: Staff Writer November 17, 2026
Chile’s copper production is forecast to fall below five million tonnes this year for the first time since 2003, as lower ore grades and operational disruptions curb output while expensive imported sulphuric acid squeezes leaching operations.
Output is expected to decline 8.4% to 4.935 million tonnes in 2026, a loss of about 453,000 tonnes from last year, the Chilean Copper Commission (Cochilco) projects in its latest forecast . It expects a 3% recovery to 5.084 million tonnes in 2027.
“Higher input costs, notably diesel and sulphuric acid, are placing upward pressure on costs,” Capstone Copper (TSX: CS; ASX: CSC) said in its July 30 results.
The world’s largest copper-producing nation faces pressure at both ends of the production chain. Ageing deposits require more ore to be processed for each tonne of metal, while reduced smelting activity limits domestic supplies of the acid used to recover copper through leaching.
Acid cuts
At Mantoverde, Capstone changed its mine plan to prioritize sulphide production and reduce leaching of ore that consumes large amounts of acid. The change cut expected acid requirements by about 200,000 tonnes, eliminating additional spot purchases for the remainder of 2026, the company said in July.
Capstone maintained its overall cost guidance at that time, citing a greater share of lower-cost sulphide production and higher byproduct credits. Its response illustrates why the impact of higher acid prices varies between operations.
Chile produced about 385,100 tonnes of copper in September, down 15% from a year earlier. Output during the first nine months declined 8.5% to 3.633 million tonnes, according to Cochilco’s monthly data.
September production fell 21% at Escondida, operated by BHP (ASX: BHP; NYSE: BHP) with Rio Tinto (LSE: RIO; NYSE: RIO) as a partner, and 27% at BHP’s wholly owned Spence mine. Output rose 17% at state-owned Codelco’s El Teniente and 7.1% at Los Pelambres, which is 60%-owned by Antofagasta (LSE: ANTO).
Lower grades, maintenance and weather disruptions have constrained output. El Teniente has also faced restrictions following its fatal 2025 rockburst, although its September production improved against the accident-affected period a year earlier.
Cochilco’s 2026 forecast would leave Chile about 900,000 tonnes below its 2018 peak of 5.832 million tonnes. The projected recovery next year would replace only about a third of this year’s decline.
Acid dependence
Chile imported a record 3.97 million tonnes of sulphuric acid in 2025, exceeding domestic production and supplying about half of national consumption. Domestic output fell 17% to 3.92 million tonnes, its lowest level since 2002, Cochilco said in its acid market study.
The closure of Ventanas, suspension of Paipote and shutdown of Potrerillos, alongside disruptions at El Teniente, reduced acid production. Chilean smelters operated at about 60% of capacity on average in 2025, according to Cochilco.
Smelters make sulphuric acid by capturing sulphur-bearing gases released during copper processing. The acid is used to dissolve copper from ore before solvent extraction and electrowinning recover the metal as cathodes.
China supplied 37% of Chile’s acid imports in 2025 before restricting exports from May 2026. Disruptions to sulphur shipments through the Strait of Hormuz also raised costs for acid producers overseas, increasing pressure on Chile’s imported supplies.
Chile sustained supplies by buying from alternative sources, including Peru, Bulgaria and South Korea, and adding India as a supplier. China authorized an exceptional shipment of about 32,000 tonnes to Chile in September, but Cochilco cautioned that this did not represent a general reopening of exports.
Contracts cushion costs
The spot price at Mejillones in northern Chile rose from about $190 per tonne in late February to $500 in late April. Many large miners had signed contracts for 2026 at $160–$175 before the disruption, limiting their exposure to the surge, according to Cochilco.
Using Chile’s 2023 average acid consumption intensity, GEM Mining Consulting calculated that the acid input cost rose from about 42¢ per lb. of copper produced through solvent extraction and electrowinning to 73¢, comparing the 2025 average import price with July 2026 prices. That is an illustrative 74% increase in the acid component, rather than in total production costs.
Actual exposure depends on ore characteristics and supply contracts. Acid consumption ranged from 0.78 to 22.4 tonnes per tonne of cathode across operations in 2023 , Cochilco found.
Copper produced through leaching, solvent extraction and electrowinning accounts for about 21% of national output. GEM estimates that output proportionally exposed to imported acid represents about 11% of Chilean copper production, including 4% exposed to Chinese supply. Its allocation model does not identify individual mines’ suppliers.
Cochilco projects acid consumption by copper mining will rise 15%, from 6.9 million tonnes in 2025 to about 7.9 million tonnes in 2027. If domestic acid production stays at its 2025 level, the gap against mining demand alone would reach about four million tonnes. The calculation illustrates potential import requirements; it is not an official supply-demand forecast. Print
